40.0.s.en: 1. A general idea of the temple and the city:

40.0.0.en: 1 In the five and twentieth year of our captivity, in the beginning of the year, in the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after that the city was smitten, in the selfsame day the hand of the LORD was upon me, and brought me thither. 2 In the visions of God brought he me into the land of Israel, and set me upon a very high mountain, by which was as the frame of a city on the south. 3 And he brought me thither, and, behold, there was a man, whose appearance was like the appearance of brass, with a line of flax in his hand, and a measuring reed; and he stood in the gate. 4 And the man said unto me, "Son of man, behold with thine eyes, and hear with thine ears, and set thine heart upon all that I shall shew thee; for to the intent that I might shew them unto thee art thou brought hither: declare all that thou seest to the house of Israel."

40.0.1.en: The Spirit of the Lord carried the prophet Ezekiel to a very high mountain, on which was the frame of a city on the south, very spacious, and at the same time it is the house of the Lord or His temple. It was called a "city" because it is the dwelling of the people, who are sanctified by dwelling with the holy God, enjoying the glory of the Lord; and it was called the "temple" because it is the dwelling of the holy God, who gathers His people around Him, sanctifies them and is glorified in them.

40.0.2.en: The prophet Ezekiel closed his book with this vision, which he related in its precise details, which he enjoyed after a life filled with bitterness and unceasing sighing for the sinners who had turned aside from the Law of the Lord, who persisted in abominations and the shedding of blood, so that the glory of the Lord departed from their city and even from His temple itself... But the prophet Ezekiel could not have enjoyed it unless the divine Spirit carried him to the summit of a very high mountain, where He brings him into the holy city, as though the prophet were lifted up by the Holy Spirit to the heavenly places through union with the Lord Christ, who lifts us on high to the bosom of His Father. This is the goal of our faith, and this is the end of our vision, indeed this is the message of our Christ: that He releases us by the Holy Spirit to the summits of the holy mountains, lifts us up in Him to bring us into the bosom of His Father, that we may be with Him and in Him forever!

40.0.3.en: How beautiful it is that the prophet closes his message by declaring this joyful vision to his brethren who live under the humiliation of captivity, to stir up in them the memories of Zion and its temple with its holy service, so as to urge them by repentance to enter into a new temple through the Messiah the Savior. Concerning this the scholar Origen says: [Those who were taken captive said in that place: "By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion" (Ps 137:1). That is, they were not able to weep until they remembered Zion, for the remembrance of what is good makes man feel the causes of misery. If we do not remember Zion and lift up our eyes toward the Law of God and the mountains of the Holy Scripture, we shall not weep over our misery.]

40.1.0.en: He says precisely, "set me upon a very high mountain" [2], for he could not have climbed this very high mountain unless the Lord Himself carried him and lifted him to the summit of the mountain. It is the work of God Himself in us! There the prophet Ezekiel saw "as the frame of a city on the south" [2]. He did not see a city but as the frame of a city, that is, like a city, for it is not a building made by the hand of man, nor is it material and temporal, but it is like a city established by the Lord Christ Himself, for he says: "And he brought me thither, and, behold, there was a man, whose appearance was like the appearance of brass, with a line of flax in his hand, and a measuring reed; and he stood in the gate" [3]. It is the Lord Christ who by His Spirit lifts us to the summit of the holy mountain, to bring us into the divine sanctuaries so that we may dwell in the heavenly places and enjoy them. As the scholar Origen says: [Let us offer our thanks for the coming of Christ, who snatched our souls from this (earthly) spectacle and turned them to care for the heavenly things and to contemplation of spiritual realities. He tore down everything that seemed great on earth, and worked to turn the worship of the Lord from the visible to the invisible and from the temporal to the eternal.]

40.1.1.en: He saw Him with an appearance like brass, that is, full of brightness and splendor and strong, treading Satan under His feet and crushing him forever. This is what St. John the Beloved saw: "his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace" (Rev 1:15).

40.1.2.en: The prophet saw in His hand a line of flax and a measuring reed. It is that pure, clean thread (flax) which signifies His work in the life of His believers: sanctification and purity. As for the measuring reed, it signifies His keeping of His children: they are known to Him (under His measure), and no one escapes from His hand. His standing at the gate of the city is a declaration that there is no entrance to this holy city except through Him, for He is "the way, the truth, and the life." He cries out: "I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture" (Jn 10:9). There is no other name by which we enjoy salvation (Acts 4:12).

40.1.3.en: The prophet noticed that the city is built on the south because the people are now in Babylon or beside it, at the river Chebar, that is, captive to a people who came from the north, so He returns them to their country, the Promised Land, in the south.

40.2.0.en: "And behold a wall on the outside of the house round about, and in the man's hand a measuring reed of six cubits long by the cubit and an hand breadth:

40.2.1.en: so he measured the breadth of the building, one reed; and the height, one reed" [5].

40.2.2.en: The first thing Ezekiel saw in this holy city or temple of the Lord is the outer wall, for God gives us His Holy Spirit as a wall of fire that keeps the human soul holy for Him, so that nothing strange or unclean may approach it, and His divine Spirit Himself keeps it on every side.

40.2.3.en: This wall also represents the Spirit of truth and discernment, the Spirit who separates the holy, divine life from the worldly life bound to the love of temporal things. For it befits the believer, in order to live holy to the Lord, to have this divine Spirit who leads him to the knowledge of truth and distinguishes it from falsehood, who knows the righteousness of Christ and distinguishes it from the evil life, so that he accepts in it what is true and what is of Christ, preventing the entrance of what is foreign to the Spirit of truth, who is the Spirit of Christ.

40.2.4.en: It is written in the book of the prophet Zechariah: "For I, saith the LORD, will be unto her a wall of fire round about, and will be the glory in the midst of her" (Zech 2:5). All the fiery darts of the enemy cannot pierce it!

40.2.5.en: As for the measuring reed, two explanations have been found for the truth of its length. The first opinion, which many prefer, is that the length of the reed is six cubits, each cubit equal to an ordinary cubit plus a hand breadth, that is, about 22 inches; and the other opinion is that the measuring reed is 6 ordinary cubits with one hand breadth added to the whole.

40.3.0.en: 6 Then came he unto the gate which looketh toward the east, and went up the stairs thereof, and measured the threshold of the gate, which was one reed broad; and the other threshold of the gate, which was one reed broad. 7 And every little chamber was one reed long, and one reed broad; and between the little chambers were five cubits; and the threshold of the gate by the porch of the gate within was one reed. 8 He measured also the porch of the gate within, one reed. 9 Then measured he the porch of the gate, eight cubits; and the posts thereof, two cubits; and the porch of the gate was inward. 10 And the little chambers of the gate eastward were three on this side, and three on that side; they three were of one measure: and the posts had one measure on this side and on that side. 11 And he measured the breadth of the entry of the gate, ten cubits; and the length of the gate, thirteen cubits. 12 The space also before the little chambers was one cubit on this side, and the space was one cubit on that side: and the little chambers were six cubits on this side, and six cubits on that side. 13 He measured then the gate from the roof of one little chamber to the roof of another: the breadth was five and twenty cubits, door against door. 14 He made also posts of threescore cubits, even unto the post of the court round about the gate. 15 And from the face of the gate of the entrance unto the face of the porch of the inner gate were fifty cubits. 16 And there were narrow windows to the little chambers, and to their posts within the gate round about, and likewise to the arches: and windows were round about inward: and upon each post were palm trees.

40.3.1.en: The main gate is the east gate, since it is the natural way leading to the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies. Yet there are two other gates, one on the north side and the other on the south, with the same measurements as the east gate, so that the whole world may enter the sanctuaries of the Lord without distinction between one nation and another, or one race and another. These three gates signify the Holy Trinity, through whom the world enters the holy city, the Jerusalem above, or into union with Him, for man is united with the Father in His Son by His Holy Spirit. These gates remind us of the twelve gates of the heavenly Jerusalem (Rev 21:13), three gates on each side... They carry a universal call to all the believers in the whole world to enjoy the divine glories through the Holy Trinity. As the Lord says: "That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven" (Mt 8:11).

40.3.2.en: On the side of each of the three gates there are six chambers, three chambers on one side and three on the other. They are small, equal chambers used for guarding. If the holy building signifies the believing soul united with the Father in His Son by His Holy Spirit to be a sanctuary for the Holy Trinity, then these chambers signify the continual guarding of the soul on every side or at every gate: the gate of the spirit, the gate of the mind, the gate of the body, so that nothing defiled or unclean may approach the spirit, the thought, or the body with its senses and energies, but the Lord Himself enters to sanctify man in his entirety: spirit, mind and body. As the Lord Himself says: "Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh" (Mt 25:13).

40.3.3.en: If God is the wall of the soul, and He is the gate, then He is also the guard of the soul, without denying the responsibility of the soul and its positive role in vigilance and strict guarding, not only by guarding against evil but also by accepting the entrance of its Lord Jesus Christ into it, that it may enjoy a constant union with Him.

40.3.4.en: These small chambers have narrow windows around the chamber, on the posts and in the arches. These small windows surround the chamber, and through them the guard looks out as well as in, and upward, and sees the firmament of heaven. It is as though the chambers are not only for guarding but also for enlightenment: enlightenment by the high heavenly things, enlightenment of the inner soul and also enlightenment of the outward conduct. Truly they are small windows, because they are counted very weak when compared with our enlightenment when we cross over into heaven itself.

40.3.5.en: The decoration of the posts with palm trees is a reference to the righteous, for "The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree" (Ps 92:11). The palm was used as a unit in the decoration of Solomon's temple (1 Kgs 6:29), and its branches were used as a sign of victory (Jn 12:13; Rev 7:9).

40.3.6.en: As for the roof of the chambers, it was in the form of a vault, signifying that everything in man should bear the heavenly character.

40.4.0.en: 17 Then brought he me into the outward court, and, lo, there were chambers, and a pavement made for the court round about: thirty chambers were upon the pavement. 18 And the pavement by the side of the gates over against the length of the gates was the lower pavement. 19 Then he measured the breadth from the forefront of the lower gate unto the forefront of the inner court without, an hundred cubits eastward and northward. 20 And the gate of the outward court that looked toward the north, he measured the length thereof, and the breadth thereof. 21 And the little chambers thereof were three on this side and three on that side; and the posts thereof and the arches thereof were after the measure of the first gate: the length thereof was fifty cubits, and the breadth five and twenty cubits. 22 And their windows, and their arches, and their palm trees, were after the measure of the gate that looketh toward the east; and they went up unto it by seven steps; and the arches thereof were before them. 23 And the gate of the inner court was over against the gate toward the north, and toward the east; and he measured from gate to gate an hundred cubits. 24 After that he brought me toward the south, and behold a gate toward the south: and he measured the posts thereof and the arches thereof according to these measures. 25 And there were windows in it and in the arches thereof round about, like those windows: the length was fifty cubits, and the breadth five and twenty cubits. 26 And there were seven steps to go up to it, and the arches thereof were before them: and it had palm trees, one on this side, and another on that side, upon the posts thereof. 27 And there was a gate in the inner court toward the south: and he measured from gate to gate toward the south an hundred cubits.

40.4.1.en: Around the court is a walk with thirty chambers for the people to use on the days of feasts, and its gates are raised by seven steps.

40.5.0.en: 28 And he brought me to the inner court by the south gate: and he measured the south gate according to these measures; 29 And the little chambers thereof, and the posts thereof, and the arches thereof, according to these measures: and there were windows in it and in the arches thereof round about: it was fifty cubits long, and five and twenty cubits broad. 30 And the arches round about were five and twenty cubits long, and five cubits broad. 31 And the arches thereof were toward the utter court; and palm trees were upon the posts thereof: and the going up to it had eight steps. 32 And he brought me into the inner court toward the east: and he measured the gate according to these measures. 33 And the little chambers thereof, and the posts thereof, and the arches thereof, were according to these measures: and there were windows therein and in the arches thereof round about: it was fifty cubits long, and five and twenty cubits broad. 34 And the arches thereof were toward the utter court; and palm trees were upon the posts thereof, on this side, and on that side: and the going up to it had eight steps. 35 And he brought me to the north gate, and measured it according to these measures; 36 The little chambers thereof, the posts thereof, and the arches thereof, and the windows to it round about: the length was fifty cubits, and the breadth five and twenty cubits. 37 And the posts thereof were toward the utter court; and palm trees were upon the posts thereof, on this side, and on that side: and the going up to it had eight steps. 38 And the chambers and the entries thereof were by the posts of the gates, where they washed the burnt offering.

40.5.1.en: a. To enter the outer court, man is bound to ascend seven steps. But entering the inner court requires ascending eight steps [31, 34,37], for the nearer man draws to the divine Presence, the more he must rise, ascending by the Holy Spirit toward the heavenly places.

40.5.2.en: If the people must ascend the seven steps to enter the outer court, then the priests, in order to enter the inner court, must ascend, beyond the seven steps, eight further steps. The priest is bound not to live like the people but to have deeper experiences and a shining heavenly conduct, that he may be truly counted a servant of the Lord.

40.5.3.en: St. Jerome paid much attention to the seven steps of the outer court and the eight steps of the inner court. He saw in the first a reference to the Old Testament and in the second a reference to the New Testament, and by adding the two together the total is fifteen steps, a reference to the Psalms of Ascents, which we chant and which lead us from step to step until they bring us into the Kingdom of Heaven.

40.5.4.en: For this reason those who cut the stones to build the house were 70,000, 80,000 men (1 Kgs 5:15), that is, the men of the Old Testament and the men of the New Testament who build the one holy house, as the holy temple of God.

40.5.5.en: St. Jerome says: [The temple has 15 steps; the high priest stands on the first step, then the priests, then the Levites.] He also says: [Consider how this temple is a pattern of the heavenly temple, for "one star differeth from another star in glory. So also is the resurrection of the dead" (1 Cor 15:41-42). Blessed is the man who is worthy to be found on the fifteenth step in the heavenly Jerusalem in the temple, for this height is exalted; I think it is the place of the Apostles and martyrs. Let us then pray that we may be made worthy to be found at least on the lowest steps of the temple of the Lord. They stand on the different steps of the temple so as to chant together in unity one psalm and one thanksgiving to the Lord. The places are different, but the praise (glorification) of the Lord is one. This concerns the heavenly Jerusalem; as for the present, we have been placed in this world to be disciplined, I think, every day of our life. One of us is on the first step; let him take courage to reach the next step. Another is on the second step; let him not lose his hope of reaching the third step! Blessed are the martyrs who were made worthy to ascend the highest steps, at the very summit; but we, living in this world, cannot ascend all the steps at once from the lowest step to the highest; rather it befits us not to stop at remaining on the first step but to struggle to reach the higher steps... I think this is the meaning of Jacob's ladder, which he saw when Jacob fled from Esau his brother.]

40.5.6.en: Perhaps St. Jerome saw in the seven steps a reference to the Old Testament because the number 7 signifies perfection, and the Law of the Lord is perfect and without blemish. As for the number 8, it refers to the New Testament because it is a symbol of the first day after the week, that is, the new heavenly life, or the risen life (for the Lord rose on the first day of the week). We have previously explained the symbolism of the numbers 7 and 8 in more than one context.

40.6.0.en: 39 And in the porch of the gate were two tables on this side, and two tables on that side, to slay thereon the burnt offering and the sin offering and the trespass offering. 40 And at the side without, as one goeth up to the entry of the north gate, were two tables; and on the other side, which was at the porch of the gate, were two tables. 41 Four tables were on this side, and four tables on that side, by the side of the gate; eight tables, whereupon they slew their sacrifices. 42 And the four tables were of hewn stone for the burnt offering, of a cubit and an half long, and a cubit and an half broad, and one cubit high: whereupon also they laid the instruments wherewith they slew the burnt offering and the sacrifice. 43 And within were hooks, an hand broad, fastened round about: and upon the tables was the flesh of the offering. 44 And without the inner gate were the chambers of the singers in the inner court, which was at the side of the north gate; and their prospect was toward the south: one at the side of the east gate having the prospect toward the north.

40.6.1.en: Eight tables of hewn stone were found, on which the burnt offering, the sin offering and the trespass offering are slain, and they signify the heavenly, spiritual sacrifices, for, as we have said, the number 8 signifies the heavenly life, or what is beyond the present time. These sacrifices are offered in the heavenly Christ Jesus after the washing of the heart and the hands, the inner purification of soul and body together.

40.7.s.en: 7. The chambers of the singers and the priests:

40.7.0.en: 45 And he said unto me, "This chamber, whose prospect is toward the south, is for the priests, the keepers of the charge of the house. 46 And the chamber whose prospect is toward the north is for the priests, the keepers of the charge of the altar: these are the sons of Zadok among the sons of Levi, which come near to the LORD to minister unto him." 47 So he measured the court, an hundred cubits long, and an hundred cubits broad, foursquare; and the altar that was before the house.

40.7.1.en: Chambers were found for the singers and others for the priests, for the sacrifice of the New Testament is bound to continual praise through the sacrifice of the Lord Christ. They are two inseparable and complementary works: the sacrifice of praise and the liturgy of the Eucharist, indeed they are one work; they are one spiritual, heavenly praise, or say one spiritual liturgy.

40.8.0.en: 48 And he brought me to the porch of the house, and measured each post of the porch, five cubits on this side, and five cubits on that side: and the breadth of the gate was three cubits on this side, and three cubits on that side. 49 The length of the porch was twenty cubits, and the breadth eleven cubits; and he brought me by the steps whereby they went up to it: and there were pillars by the posts, one on this side, and another on that side.

40.8.1.en: A porch of the house was found, through which we enter the sanctuaries, so that no one may approach the presence of God rashly and hastily, but with reverence; he passes through the porch quietly, to forget all his thoughts about temporal matters and prepare for contemplation of the heavenly and divine things.

40.8.2.en: Establish in me Your holy temple!

40.8.3.en: * What does my soul desire but that You dwell in it, O my Savior, and make it Your holy temple, made by Your hands?!

40.8.4.en: Turn my heart into a holy city, in which the angels of Your angels gather with Your saints in Your presence!

40.8.5.en: And establish in it Your holy temple, in which the soul worships You, rejoicing with Your creation!

40.8.6.en: * Come down into my depths, and make of them the very high mountain that Ezekiel Your prophet saw.

40.8.7.en: There You hold in Your hand a line of flax and a measuring reed.

40.8.8.en: For You are the One who measures the temple and determines its dimensions!

40.8.9.en: You are its Builder and its Sanctifier!

40.8.10.en: * How beautiful is that wall with which You surround Your house?!

40.8.11.en: It is the wall of fire; all the fiery darts of the enemy cannot pierce it!

40.8.12.en: You are my wall and the fortress of my life!

40.8.13.en: * What are the three gates through which all the nations enter but You, O Holy Trinity?!

40.8.14.en: For we are all united with the Father in His Son by the Holy Spirit!

40.8.15.en: This is the true gate: our Trinitarian faith!

40.8.16.en: By it we enjoy the life of worship, by it we live in the heavenly places!

40.8.17.en: * On both sides of each gate are six chambers for guarding, three on this side and three on that!

40.8.18.en: It is the Trinitarian faith that guards the soul, the body and the spirit!

40.8.19.en: O Trinity, sanctify my body with all its senses!

40.8.20.en: And my soul with all its powers!

40.8.21.en: And my spirit with all its capabilities!

40.8.22.en: That I may be wholly kept by You and sanctified to You!

40.8.23.en: * You are wonderful, O my God!

40.8.24.en: You are the gate, and You are the guard!

40.8.25.en: By You I enter the sanctuaries, and in You I take refuge from the opposing enemy!

40.8.26.en: * What are these many windows in the building but a sign of vigilance, from which the watchful guard looks out?!

40.8.27.en: They are a sign of enlightenment; through them we see the pledge of the heavenly places!

40.8.29.en: It is of palm trees, a sign of victory and enlightenment!

40.8.31.en: It is a sign of the heavenly life in us!

40.8.32.en: * Grant me, O Lord, hope, that I may ascend the steps, that I may rise on the seven steps of the outer court as Your believers rose in the Old Testament, seeking perfection!

40.8.33.en: And that I may rise on the eight steps of the inner court as Your Apostles rose in the New Testament, seeking what is beyond time!

40.8.34.en: * Let eight heavenly tables be established within me, that my soul may be satisfied with You, O unique Sacrifice!

40.8.35.en: Teach me that my heart may be washed and purified by Your blood, and so be made worthy of Your feast forever!

40.8.36.en: * Establish, O Lord, the chambers of the singers and the chambers of the priests, that praise may be joined to the sacrifice, and my life be turned into a holy liturgy!

40.8.37.en: * Establish a porch in which I may walk quietly, through which I enter into Your temple, and by passing through it I cast temporal things aside and contemplate the heavenly places!

40.8.38.en: * How wonderful You are, who establish Your temple in me!

40.8.39.en: How sweet You are, who dwell within me!
